### 2026-10-25: So I'm doing everything over the weekend due to tests, aside from that. After the previous lapses, the issue I faced was that when I uploaded the footprint for the diode it would just disappear, the

**1.4h**

So I'm doing everything over the weekend due to tests, aside from that. After the previous lapses, the issue I faced was that when I uploaded the footprint for the diode it would just disappear, the  3d model would be there, but it would just disappear on the  PCB editor.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 190028](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Aak0Y0a0ppmv3RPoHNE55PGI9i4P30aq/11de7f5d87d8400613302aff8c1c863e35e01f87d74fd148e7a404fde17efe49.png)
This is very bad. The main way I fixed it was that to keep the 3D model of the old diodes the same, but update only the ones for the switches so that. This meant that while the PCB editor will have the diodes, the 3D model will not.
This is the before and after

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 174954](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Aak0Y0a0ppmv3RPoHNE55PGI9i4P30aq/73f58e98a4f796424f460a396bf7b18eea6aceeab215156ebc0a5094ad95328d.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 184705](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Aak0Y0a0ppmv3RPoHNE55PGI9i4P30aq/65f300fb69daeeb98923842e65f912dd3c1d3f888828190cb04562cb08949047.png)
There is no other way to solve it that I found without me having to do lots of wiring again, even if the proper Footprint editor comes in.
Overall it was still fine, and everything still works, there are no errors, just warnings that the model for Diodes is out of sync.
TLDR;Diodes disappeared due to an issue with the footprint library, the only efficient way to solve it was to keep the Diode footprint the same, resulting in a generic 3D model, but keeping the whole PCB intact in the PCB editor.

### 2026-10-25: In this session(prior to dinner), I refined the PCB a bit then worked on getting sounds for the keyboard.

**2.5h**

In this session(prior to dinner), I refined the PCB a bit then worked on getting sounds for the keyboard.
The Microprocessor used is the Raspberry Pi Pico 2, with the help of a speaker and an amp. It should be able to support mp3 files.

So I got a set of mp3 files from a GitHub repo, it has 136 audio files covering all the notes of the piano even possibly playable.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 224934](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Aak0Y0a0ppmv3RPoHNE55PGI9i4P30aq/ce93075660cbbf8698f56b517f99a19928b53ba567a92ee011db6df654b18fd4.png)
Now the main issue with these files was the size. The Pico2 has 4mb of space generally, but about 1-1.5mb is taken up by circuit python. So I had around 2.5mb to work with, after trying out a few compressor sites I managed to compress the files to much much lesser than their initial size

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 224835](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Aak0Y0a0ppmv3RPoHNE55PGI9i4P30aq/8d354319903737c555322c18e22f6c9bf6664d900271f91b0a2038aa64b36346.png)

Much lesser as in about a quarter, now the size comes down to around 2.75Mb!! Which should most likely fit in the Pico 2.

Following that, I decided to make the mp3 into .wav files so that incase it doesn't support mp3, I should still be able to play sounds. Now the conversion for this is the the cause of around 1.5 hours of this time. This is because  I couldn't find any good sites that could allow for mass conversion and couldn't get ffmpeg to work until near the end of all of this (Still it resulted in me saving time since I had only finished around 95 files.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 224735](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Aak0Y0a0ppmv3RPoHNE55PGI9i4P30aq/2f68169ad3615bb54e107a0061380e2ad0973a1d12a5c7cadc73fe6360f1f0f0.png)

Sidestory:Now the main issue with those is their size. I tried to compress them using a site, but it could only do 1 at a time and when I tried to do several at once. I accidentally opened 136 TABS and had to fight desperately to close em all(With a dying ram in the background) I couldn't take a pic of that cause my laptop started freezing and sounding like a jet.

TLDR; Found mp3files for the noises the keyboard should make, compressed all the files to a small enough size that they can fit in the storage of the Raspberry Pi Pico 2,Converted all the mp3 files to .wav files, Had to close 136 tabs as my laptop died in the background

### 2026-10-25: This was a session(Post dinner) where I mainly dealt with the firmware aspect of it.Now the main struggle here was that I am using a Raspberry Pi Pico 2, which is great and it runs circuit python, I'v

**3h**

This was a session(Post dinner) where I mainly dealt with the firmware aspect of it.Now the main struggle here was that I am using a Raspberry Pi Pico 2, which is great and it runs circuit python, I've never worked with circuit python and also suck at coding.
To deal with this major issue, I decided to use every resource I could find, In this case, Perplixity,Gemini,Claude and Youtube. I used Perplexity mainly just to get info on which videos will help out.Next On Youtube,I found "Build With Prof. G.", who is now my hero. He had a series on coding for circuit python for the Raspberry Pi Pico 2,AND ITS A GREAT SERIES!! It's honestly great and very helpful and informative, he also has the series for several other circuit python related things and has criminally less views.  I mainly decided to type a lot of code using his vids as reference

The issue was that by now it was around 9:15 IST so I decided to code using some of his vids and consult with Gemini and Claude to make the code more efficient instead of walls of meaningless text. This resulted in several hours of confusion and chaos. Now the main thing is I used Mu editor for the code and the only real way to test is by having the Raspberry Pi Pico 2.Aside from that spent several hours messing around in code until all the 'ai's agreed the code looks fine,Cause that's all I could consult
